title: Settings page navigation overhaul: replace 28-panel vertical list with tabbed category navigation
goal: The Settings screen currently renders 28 collapsible panels in a single vertical list. Visual audit 2026-05-03 shows this produces a page that scrolls for over 10 viewport heights with no visual grouping. Operators cannot quickly find what they need. Redesign: (1) Add a tab bar at the top of the Settings content area with 5 tabs: 'AI & Provider' (ChatGPT OAuth, AI provider), 'Tools & Runtime' (readiness, execution, concurrency, scheduled scans, tool paths), 'Integrations' (Jira, SIEM, CI/CD, webhooks, repositories), 'Data & Security' (retention, encryption, hardening, backup), 'Identity & Users' (users, API keys, SSO). (2) Each tab shows only the panels relevant to that category — maximum 6 panels per tab. (3) Keep the expand/collapse behaviour within each tab. (4) Add a prominent search/filter input at the top of Settings ('Find a setting...') that highlights matching panels across all tabs. The existing DEFAULT_SETTINGS_PANELS object and panel rendering in settings.js must be preserved; only add tab routing and the search box.
scope: Visual audit 2026-05-03: ui/test-results/visual-audit-2026-05-03/02-settings-initial.png shows 28 vertically stacked panels taking over 10x viewport height. No visual grouping or navigation. Enterprise operators spending 30+ seconds finding a single setting is unacceptable.
generation_reason: Visual audit 2026-05-03: 28 flat panels in settings is overwhelming — add tab navigation and search.

Each tab shows only the panels relevant to its category.

All existing panels accessible via tabs.
